chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I said to him, 'May I be your ransom, do the Muslims have an Eid other than the two Eids?' He said, 'Yes, O Hasan, the greatest and most noble of them.'
I said, 'And which day is it?' He said, 'It is the day when the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) raised a standard for the people.'

So I said, 'May I be your ransom, and what is appropriate for us to do on it?' He said, 'Fast it, O Hasan, and increase your prayers upon Muhammad and his family on it, and declare your disassociation to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, from those who wronged them.'
And indeed, the Prophets (peace be upon them) used to command the Successors regarding the day on which the Successor is established, that it be taken as an Eid.'
I said, 'So what is the reward for the one who fasts it?' He said, 'The fasting of sixty months.'

And do not neglect the fasting of the twenty-seventh of Rajab, for it is the day on which Prophethood descended upon Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), and its reward is like that of sixty months for you.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)
key_terms.الْعِيدَيْنِ: The two Eids (Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the day other than the two Eids in Shia tradition, and what are its prescribed acts of worship?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* identifies the day of Ghadir (or the establishment of the Imamate) as a major Eid, prescribing fasting, abundant Salawat, and *Tawalli wa Tabarri* (affiliation and disassociation) as key acts of worship. It uniquely links this celebration to the prophetic tradition of appointing successors, while also highlighting the 27th of Rajab as the day of Prophethood's descent, offering a reward equivalent to sixty months of fasting for those who fast it.
